minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Agency,
  Community Development Financing Authority,
  Public Improvement Corporation,
  and Library Board of Trustees*

  October 19, 2009

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Agency, the Community
Development Financing Authority, the Public Improvement Corporation, and the Library Board
of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Ury at 5:02
p.m., on October 19, 2009, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on October 16, 2009, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the
Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Kelley (arrived at 5:07 p.m.)
  Council Member Ledesma
  Council Member Schlicht (arrived at 5:03 p.m.)
  Mayor Pro Tem MacLean
  Mayor Ury

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  Irwin B. Bornstein, Assistant City Manager/Director of Admin. Services
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

INVOCATION: Mayor Ury

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Ledesma

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with City Attorney Concerning One matter of Existing Litigation
  Pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.9(a). The Litigation is City of Mission
  Viejo v. Saddleback Valley Unified School District (SVUSD), Case No. 00300610.

City Council Minutes  1  October 19, 2009
 CS2. Conference with City Attorney Concerning One matter of Existing Litigation
  Pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.9(a). The Litigation is City of Mission
  Viejo v. Capistrano Unified School District (CUSD), Case No. 00180049;
  Companion Case, Rancho Santa Margarita v. CUSD, Case No. 00207543.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:03 p.m., Mayor Ury recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council
reconvened at 6:01 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that there was nothing to report from Closed Session.

PRESENTATIONS

Items P1, P2 and P3 were taken out of order.

P2.  Poseidon Resources Desalination Facility Presentation

  The City Council received the presentation from Scott Maloni, Vice President of
  Poseidon Resources.

  By consensus, the City Council directed staff to return with a resolution of support at the
  next City Council Meeting.

P3.  Presentation by the Mission Viejo Activities Committee, "Keeping a Light on a
  Mission Viejo Holiday Tradition"

  The City Council received the presentation from Dave Breazeale from the Mission Viejo
  Activities Committee.

P1.  Presentation by the Orange County Fire Authority for Acts of Heroism Awards

  Mayor Ury, Council Member Kelley, Battalion Chief Scott Brown and Fire
  Captain/Paramedic Steve Concialdi presented awards to Nathan Navarro and Chasen
  Radison for their heroism during a traffic accident on the 5 freeway near La Paz. Spencer
  Owen was unable to attend the meeting and the presentation to Shawn Alladio was
  delayed (see Presentations Continued.)

City Council Minutes  2  October 19, 2009
 PUBLIC COMMENTS

Judy Iannaccone and George Avila, Board Members of OC Human Relations, Santa Ana:
outlined the role of their organization throughout the County, particularly in Mission Viejo, and
presented a copy of the OC Human Relations Annual Report.

Claudia Divito, Rancho Santa Margarita: announced that the Cultural Arts Committee is seeking
32 images depicting the spirit of thankfulness and caring for the Mission Viejo Parkway Gallery.
Residents can upload their photographs at www.cityofmissionviejo.org/uploads.

PRESENTATIONS (Continued)

P1.  Presentation by the Orange County Fire Authority for Acts of Heroism Awards
  (Continued)

  Mayor Ury, Council Member Kelley, Battalion Chief Scott Brown and Fire
  Captain/Paramedic Steve Concialdi presented the award to Shawn Alladio for her
  heroism during a traffic accident on the 5 freeway near La Paz.

PUBLIC COMMENTS (Continued)

Larry Gilbert, M.V.: provided a history of the Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center
expansion project and asked how we ended up spending $15.5 million on the project.

The following spoke in support of a Mission Viejo dog park: Dr. Philip Glaser, M.V. and Pat
Clay, M.V.

The following spoke in support of a dog park at Oso Viejo Community Park: Sarah Grimberg,
M.V.; Corissa Sellers, M.V.; Susan Sellers, M.V.; Ron Ruef, M.V.; and Meredith Rushing.

The following spoke in opposition to a dog park at Oso Viejo Community Park: Myron Sipp,
M.V. (presented a petition signed by over 200 residents opposed to a dog park at Oso Viejo
Community Park) Christa Hattem, M.V.; Alia Noumiller, M.V.; Dave Gove, M.V.; Karen
Medeiros, M.V.; Melora Vandersluis, M.V.; and Mary Holley.

The following spoke in favor of a dog park and in opposition to placing one at the Animal
Shelter: Carl Lekander, M.V.; Nancy Teel, M.V.; and Sharon Cody, M.V.

The following presented written comments in opposition to a dog park at Oso Viejo Community

City Council Minutes  3  October 19, 2009
 Park: Norm Neumiller, M.V.; Karen Medeiros, M.V.; Lisa Moreno, M.V.; J.C. Moreno, M.V.;
Lara Sipp, M.V.; Dawn Gove, M.V.; and Dane Kovacs, M.V.

The following presented written comments in opposition to a dog park at the Animal Shelter:
Denise Singh, M.V. and Dianne Doyle, Laguna Niguel.

Robert Reidel, M.V.: stated that he is against the proposed change to the way in which
Capistrano Unified School District Trustees are elected.

Connie Lee, M.V.: read from a resolution adopted by the Saddleback Republican Committee
supporting the recall of Mayor Pro Tem MacLean.

David Allen, M.V.: expressed opposition to the recall of Mayor Pro Tem MacLean and stated
that the effort is a personal attack by a small group of people. Mr. Allen suggested that the
money could be better used for City facilities that benefit all and he encouraged voters to get
involved and understand the facts.

COUNCIL COMMENTS

Council Member Kelley

28.  OCTA Bus Service Reductions

  Council Member Kelley presented the report.

  Paul Glaab, OCTA Board of Directors and City Council Member of Laguna Niguel:
  discussed OCTA’s budget challenges and the reason for the proposed service reduction
  strategies.

  Michael E. Bailey, M.V.: stated that he supports a Council Member attending the October
  26th OCTA public hearing to testify on behalf of the City.

  The following presented a written comment in support of Option B: Alex Lewis, M.V.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Ledesma,
  to direct staff to send a letter to OCTA regarding the proposed bus route reductions and
  requesting that OCTA not reduce or eliminate any bus service in the City or, if some
  reduction is necessary, that it be in the form of reduced trips (Strategy B or some

City Council Minutes  4  October 19, 2009
   variation thereof) rather than elimination of routes or weekend service.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

  Mayor Ury asked Council Member Kelley to attend and speak on behalf of Mission Viejo
  at the OCTA public hearing on October 26, 2009, to discuss impacts of the proposed
  reductions on Mission Viejo residents.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Item 3 was removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.

Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Ledesma, to approve
the Consent Calendar as described below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said
  titles which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title
  and further reading waived.

2.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the Regular Meeting of October 5, 2009, as presented.

4.  Check Register dated September 25, 2009, in the amount of $1,970,062.73

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  Check Register dated October 2, 2009, in the amount of $617,401.34

City Council Minutes  5  October 19, 2009
   Ratified the accompanying check register.

6.  City Treasurer's Monthly Report for August 2009

  Received and filed.

7.  Community Development Agency Treasurer's Monthly Report for August 2009

  Received and filed.

8.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority (MVCDFA)
  Treasurer's Monthly Report for August 2009

  Received and filed.

9.  Landscape and Irrigation Materials and Supplies Purchase Agreement Bonding
  Requirements Clarification

  Approved Fourth Amendment to John Deere Landscapes, Inc. and First Amendment to
  Hydro-Scape Products, Inc. purchase agreements clarifying that no performance bond or
  labor and material bond is required.

10.  Annual Routine Monthly Landscape & Facility Maintenance - Contract Area 6

  (1) Awarded the contract for the subject services to Nieves Landscape, Inc. for the period
  November 1, 2009, through June 30, 2011, in the amount of $631,504.00 and; (2)
  authorized staff to issue a purchase order to Nieves Landscape, Inc. for the period
  November 1, 2009, through June 30, 2010, in an amount not to exceed $252,714.00.

11.  Annual Maintenance Program for the Repair and Reconstruction of Streets,
  Drainage Channels, Storm Drains, Slopes, and Emergency Response.

  (1) Awarded contract for the subject program to L.T. Engineering for the period of
  November 1, 2009, to June 30, 2011, in an amount not to exceed $275,000.00; (2)
  authorized the issuance of a purchase order for the period of November 1, 2009, through
  June 30, 2010, in an amount not to exceed $130,000.00; and (3) approved license
  agreement with LT Engineering for the period of November 1, 2009, through June 30,
  2011.

12.  Annual Review of Residential and Commercial Integrated Waste Management Rates

City Council Minutes  6  October 19, 2009
   Adopted Resolution 09-46 Approving the Proposed Trash Rate Adjustment for
  Residential (0.1% increase from $13.99 to $14.00 per Month), Commercial (0.4%
  Decrease), and Roll-Off (0.4% Decrease) Services Effective January 1, 2010.

13.  Fiber Communication and Traffic Controller Upgrade Project-Various Locations
  (CIP 797)

  Awarded the contract to Crosstown Electrical & Data, Inc., in the amount of $42,740 for
  the installation of conduits and fiber optic cable.

14.  Crown Valley Parkway Widening Improvements (CIP 752)

  Authorized reimbursement of the initial deposit in the amount of $500,000 to DMB
  Ladera, L.L.C., for the Crown Valley Parkway Widening Improvements.

15.  Crown Valley Parkway Widening, Cabot Road to I-5 (CIP 795)

  Approved the First Amendment to the agreement with the City of Laguna Niguel and
  RBF Consulting for professional design services for the Crown Valley Parkway/I-5
  Widening Project, including the City of Mission Viejo’s share of additional costs in the
  amount of $90,315 contingent upon approval of said amendment by the City of Laguna
  Niguel.

16.  Medical Center Road Pavement Resurfacing (CIP 838)

  Awarded the construction contract for the subject project to All American Asphalt, Inc.,
  in the amount of $133,321.00.

17.  Second Amendment to the Assistant City Manager/Director of Administrative
  Services Employment Agreement

  Approved the Second Amendment to the Assistant City Manager/Director of
  Administrative Services Employment Agreement.

18.  Possible Refunding of 1996 Library Certificates Of Participation and 2001 Series A
  City Hall/Library Lease Revenue Bonds

  Referred this matter to the Investment Advisory Commission for their review and
  recommendation.

City Council Minutes  7  October 19, 2009
 PUBLIC HEARINGS

OLD BUSINESS

19.  Appointment to Fill Two (2) Unscheduled Vacancies on the Planning and
  Transportation Commission

  Council Member Kelley nominated Robert Bruckmann.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem MacLean, to
  appoint Robert Bruchmann to serve on the Planning and Transportation Commission.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

  Council Member Schlicht nominated Mark Dobrilovic.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Ledesma, to
  appoint Mark Dobrilovic to serve on the Planning and Transportation Commission.

  On roll call, said motion failed by the following vote:

  AYES:  Ledesma and Schlicht
  NOES:  Kelley, MacLean and Ury
  ABSENT: None

  Council Member Schlicht stated that she will continue to interview applicants.

20.  Special Municipal Election - February 2, 2010

  City Clerk Karen Hamman presented the staff report.

  Dale Tyler, M.V.: stated that community watch dogs had high hopes that Council
  Member MacLean would initiate small, fiscally responsible government and he
  announced that recall proponents look forward to the election.

  Lisa VanWinkle, M.V.: expressed frustration that this election will cost the taxpayers

City Council Minutes  8  October 19, 2009
   $227,000, yet Council Member MacLean is up for re-election in November of the same
  year. She asked if there is anything that taxpayers can do to inform the people what it
  will cost and to reverse the election.

  Motion made by Council Member Ledesma, seconded by Council Member Schlicht, to
  (1) adopt Resolution 09-47 Calling and Giving Notice of the Holding of a Special
  Election on Tuesday, February 2, 2010, for the Submission of the Question of the Recall
  of Council Member Lance MacLean and the Election of Candidate to Fill the Vacancy if
  the Recall Prevails; (2) adopt Resolution 09-48 Requesting the Board of Supervisors of
  the County of Orange to Render Specified Services to the City Relating to the Conduct of
  a Special Municipal Election to be held on Tuesday February 2, 2010; (3) adopt
  Resolution 09-49 Adopting Regulations Pertaining to Candidates Statements Submitted
  to the Voters at an Election to be held on Tuesday, February 2, 2010; (4) direct the City
  Clerk to schedule the adoption of the resolution citing the election results and the
  administration of the oath to the newly elected Council Members for March 1, 2010, or as
  soon as possible thereafter.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, Schlicht and Ury
  NOES:  MacLean
  ABSENT: None

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht to take $227,000 from the tennis center
  improvement project budget to pay for the special election. The motion died for lack of a
  second.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Ledesma, to
  adopt Resolution 09-50 Amending the Fiscal Year 2009-2010 Budget to Pay for the
  February 2, 2010, Special Election (taking those funds from the unappropriated fund
  balance of the General Fund) for the Submission of the Question of the Recall of Council
  Member Lance MacLean and the Election of a Candidate to Fill the Vacancy if the Recall
  Prevails.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, Schlicht and Ury
  NOES:  MacLean
  ABSENT: None

City Council Minutes  9  October 19, 2009
 NEW BUSINESS

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

3.  Summary of FY 2009-10 Budget Amendments To Date

  Dave Gove, M.V.: asked that the dog park vote be reconsidered under this item in light of
  the fact that many residents are opposed to it being placed at Oso Viejo Park.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem MacLean, to
  receive and file.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

STAFF REPORTS

City Attorney’s Report

25.  Survey Results; Single School District Issue

  Adam Probolsky, Probolsky Research LLC, Laguna Hills: outlined the survey results and
  answered questions of the City Council.

  The following expressed interest in the school district survey and support for a Charter
  School at the former O'Neill Elementary School site: Robert Reidel, M.V.; Bert Bennett,
  M.V.; Kandi Brennan, M.V.; Kim Price, M.V.; Julie Collier, M.V.; Lisa VanWinkle,
  M.V.; and Linda DeFonce, M.V.

  By consensus, the City Council directed staff to send a letter to the SVUSD affirming the
  City's strong support of the past charter school application for the O'Neill School site and
  of the current charter school proposal for the Oxford Preparatory Academy of Mission
  Viejo.

26.  City Council Update Regarding 26992 La Paja

City Council Minutes  10  October 19, 2009
   City Attorney Bill Curley presented the staff report.

  Catherine Jasper, M.V.: expressed continued dissatisfaction with the lengthy construction
  project and asked why the property owner has more rights than the neighbors.

  By consensus, the City Council directed that the City Attorney advance this concept with
  the property owner's legal counsel, analyze the legal pros and cons attendant to such an
  approach, and advise the City Council in a properly agendaized Closed Session at a
  Council Meeting in November.

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, AND COMMITTEE REPORTS

21.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Council Member Kelley presented the report.

22.  Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Pro Tem MacLean presented the report.

23.  San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Council Member Ledesma presented the report.

24.  SCAG Transportation & Communications Committee (TCC) Report

  Council Member Kelley presented the report.

STAFF REPORTS (Continued)

City Manager's Report

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS (Continued)

27.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities
  calendars as presented in the staff report and agreed to provide any changes to the City

City Council Minutes  11  October 19, 2009
   Clerk for the public record.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley announced that she will be agendaizing the CUSD vote by Trustee area
matter however she thinks there is a lot more information that needs to be gathered and she
wants to find out if there are any challenges to the initiative going forward. She announced that
she does plan to put it on a future agenda and she will incorporate Mayor Pro Tem MacLean’s
suggestions at that time. Council Member Kelley outlined her participation in the walk to school
day with Bathgate Elementary students on October 7, 2009. She also discussed her attendance at
the Rachel’s Challenge presentation at Newhart Middle School on October 15, 2009. She noted
that it was very powerful and members of the community were invited to attend the same
presentation that the students heard. Many parents have shared positive feedback and reported
that their children have been dramatically impacted by the presentation. Council Member Kelley
announced that there will be another Rachel’s Challenge event on October 19, 2009, at Don Juan
Avila Middle School in Aliso Viejo at 7:00 p.m. These presentations will culminate in a
gathering of participants to show a physical chain link of kindness and she stated that it will be
interesting to see how big an impact we can make. She also discussed her attendance at the 21st
Annual Walk Against Drugs and Supervisor Pat Bates’ Disaster Preparedness Expo where she
heard many positive comments from the participants. In closing, Council Member Kelley
offered her condolences to commissioner Les Sykes who lost his wife today.

Council Member Ledesma

Council Member Schlicht

Council Member Schlicht expressed her condolences to Les Sykes and stated that we are so sorry
for his loss. In reference to the dog park, she stated that she is concerned there will be a display
of dog owners pitted against one another and she believes that was created by the Council
majority’s inconsistencies with the parameters of the dog park. She noted that the community
was told there would be another public discussion tomorrow but that has been pulled and she
expressed concern that if the request to place a training circuit around that area is fulfilled, it will
create another problem with a dog park at the Oso Viejo location. Council Member Schlicht
stated that she is sorry that the Council wouldn’t appoint Mark Dobrilovic to the Planning and
Transportation Commission and she feels there is a double standard with this City Council based
on Mayor Pro Tem MacLean past actions. She asked about a letter she received from resident
Marvis Kushnick regarding Santa’s Workshop and possible effects on the library operations.
City Manager Wilberg indicated that staff has had discussions with Ms. Kushnick and have
addressed her concerns. Council Member Schlicht outlined her attendance at the Drug Walk and

City Council Minutes  12  October 19, 2009
 announced that she looks forward to watching an upcoming Diablos football game at the same
Mission Viejo High School stadium. She announced that Dr. Frank Lieberman is starting an
organization to fight drug and alcohol abuse through the Chabad of California and she looks
forward to that success. Finally, Council Member Schlicht stated that there are still ten pages of
foreclosures in the Saddleback Valley News and since things aren’t getting better, the City has
got to watch its expenses.

Mayor Pro Tem MacLean

Mayor Pro Tem MacLean stated that we do need to watch our expenses so supporting the
expenditure of $270,000 on a recall election is like speaking out of both sides of your mouth. He
stated that he will respond to Council Member Schlicht’s misinformation and lies to the
community regarding the dog park. He recalled that this is not the first time there has been push-
back from residents and he pointed to the Montanoso traffic calming project. Some residents
were opposed to that project yet the same people are now asking that the work be completed
because it has been a success. He stated that people are spreading hyperbole by referring to the
dog park as a “bark park” and spreading lies about the cost, diseases, and water quality. He
thinks that once the dog park has been built and is being used, the residents in that area will
discover that these were just scare tactics. Mayor Pro Tem MacLean announced that he blames a
lot of the recall proponents for spreading lies and for finding hot buttons to gain support. He
noted the disrespect of members of the public who turned their back on him as he spoke this
evening and he stated that his Council colleague got up and left the dais because she didn’t want
to hear the truth.

Council Member Schlicht departed the dais at 10:32 p.m. and returned at 10:35 p.m.

Mayor Pro Tem MacLean stated that the childish behavior has got to stop and that we need to
have a city run by people who are thinking of the greater good of the community, not a small
minority of people who want to dismantle anything good. He announced that he looks forward
to fighting the recall very vigorously and he invited anyone who would like to help to contact
him by phone or by email.

Mayor Ury

29.  Placing bleacher shade covering over fields at Youth Athletic Park, Gilleran, Beebe
  and Curtis Baseball Fields

  Motion made by Mayor Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem MacLean, to direct staff to
  obtain bids for design and construction of bleacher shade covering and return at the next
  City Council Meeting

City Council Minutes  13  October 19, 2009
   On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

Mayor Ury stated that it is disappointing to see so many people come and get so inflamed over
an item like the dog park when we have spent six years researching it. He expressed concern
that Council Member Schlicht has been doing what she can to whip up the troops to create that
kind of angst and animosity. He cautioned his colleagues to reflect on how much each of them
could be responsible for creating the tension that has gone on here. Mayor Ury stated that
everyone lives with compromises and it’s tough to get 100,000 residents in a City to agree on
everything at the same time. He noted that it’s ironic that he was on the Community Services
Commission when the dog park was first discussed and moved forward. He further expressed
concern that a very vocal minority of people are coming into the City and putting the Council in
a position of worrying about moving things forward. Mayor Ury stated that the only thing we
have heard from Council Member Schlicht the entire year is “let’s put a roundabout in.” He
stated that there are certain things that need to be done in the City that the Council needs to step
up and address. He challenged his colleagues to confront the negativism with action and he
noted that Council Member Schlicht and Council Member Ledesma have decided that a recall is
their level of action. Mayor Ury recalled that he has constantly asked how much money is
enough money to have in reserves but he has never gotten a firm answer on that. He feels there
is a love affair with the bank account and at a certain point we either have enough money or we
don’t. He encouraged his colleagues to put items on the agenda if they have concerns instead of
telling the residents of Mission Viejo that fifteen or eighteen years of planning to save budgetary
reserves is not enough. Mayor Ury stated that the monetary planning certainly wasn’t because of
the people who are trying to run a recall, but it was probably in spite of them. He recommended
that the City Council Members take a look at how much they are planning on leading and how
much they are planning on complaining. Mayor Ury noted that it will be a very interesting time
ahead and he plans on addressing what he calls the unfinished needs of the residents of our City.
He announced that he is comfortable with 50% or 40% of our operating budget in reserves and
he doesn’t think things need to stop. While he agrees that things are tough in the economy, he
believes the residents have elected them because the community expects more thought than
inaction. Mayor Ury concluded by thanking all the volunteers for another successful Drug Walk.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 10:44 p.m., there being no further business to come before the Council at this

City Council Minutes  14  October 19, 2009
 session, Mayor Ury adjourned the meeting in memory of Joyce Sykes, to Monday, November 2,
2009, at 5:00 p.m.

__________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of November 2, 2009

City Council Minutes  15  October 19, 2009
